Let me carefully parse this problem. The user is asking about a "meta-token" — one content-addressed anchor resolving meaning across multiple token sets, in the "frontier-scout burn pipeline." The design goal: two independent implementations must produce byte-identical roots from the same start.

This is a cryptographic/data-structure design problem. Let me decode the terminology:

- "Meta-token": a single anchor object that carries meaning across multiple token sets (i.e., multiple vocabularies/tokenizations or multiple streams of tokens).
- "Content-addressed": its identity is derived from its content via a hash (like Git objects, IPFS CIDs, BLAKE3 hashes).
- "Anchor resolving meaning across multiple token sets": it maps/anchors semantics so that the same logical unit is identifiable regardless of which tokenization (tokenizer version, language, byte-level vs. BPE, etc.) produced the token stream.
- "Frontier-scout burn pipeline": this sounds like an agentic exploration pipeline where "scouts" explore frontier nodes and "burn" them after processing (i.e., consume and discard state). "Burn" suggests irreversibility — once burned, the scout's output is committed into some accumulator/Merkle structure and the raw state is discarded.
- "Two independent implementations produce byte-identical roots from the same start": deterministic canonical serialization + canonical hashing; the root of a Merkle structure over the pipeline's outputs must be reproducible bit-for-bit by any conforming implementation. This means: no floating point, no map iteration order dependence, no timestamps, no locale-dependent encoding, no ambiguous UTF-8 normalization, no hash-map nondeterminism, canonical JSON or better a custom binary encoding with explicit endianness, length prefixes, sorted keys, etc.

So I need to design:

1. The meta-token data structure: fields, canonical binary encoding (byte-exact).
2. Content addressing: which hash function (BLAKE3 is a good choice: fast, standardized, no ambiguity; SHA-256 also acceptable but slower; BLAKE2b/3 are fine), how the address is computed (domain separation, tag-length-value), truncation rules if any.
3. How it anchors across multiple token sets: define token set identity (each token set has a TokenSetID = H(canonical tokenizer descriptor)), and the meta-token carries per-set projections (e.g., for each token set, the list of token IDs that realize this logical symbol) plus a canonical semantic payload (the actual text/codepoints/bytes) so meaning doesn't depend on any single tokenizer.
4. The burn pipeline: stages — frontier queue → scout picks node → expands → emits tokens → tokens get normalized into meta-tokens → meta-tokens accumulate into a Merkleized log/tree → when a scout finishes/burns, its contribution is sealed with a finalization record including the running root → burned state is discarded, only the root chain survives.
5. Determinism requirements: exact rules to make two independent implementations produce identical roots:
   - Canonical serialization: TLV with fixed field order, explicit lengths, little-endian or big-endian (pick one — big-endian for network-order clarity? Actually let me pick little-endian... hmm, "no fluff" — just pick and justify briefly: pick big-endian because it matches network byte order and most spec conventions; either works as long as it's pinned. Let me pin BIG-ENDIAN and say so.)
   - Hash function: BLAKE3 with domain-separation prefixes ("OX-META-TOKEN v1" etc.). Actually maybe use SHA-256 for maximal availability and FIPS acceptance? BLAKE3 is fine and faster. The requirement is only that both implementations agree. I'll specify BLAKE3-256 (32-byte output) as primary with a mandatory algorithm ID field so future changes don't break old roots.
   - Sorting rules: all sets/maps serialized in lexicographic order of their canonical-encoded keys.
   - No floats anywhere; integers only, varint or fixed-width? Fixed-width u64/u128 avoids varint ambiguity? Varints (LEB128) are well-defined too. To be maximally unambiguous and simple: fixed widths, big-endian. Lengths as u64 BE.
   - Unicode: require input already normalized to NFC? Better: forbid text entirely at the anchor layer — carry bytes only; if text needed, carry code points as UTF-8 plus a normalization flag recorded (NFC applied before anchoring, and record the normalizer version? Simpler: mandate NFC with Unicode version pinned in the tokenizer descriptor). Hmm. The cleanest determinism rule: meta-token semantic payload is raw bytes; any text must have been normalized to NFC using Unicode version U (pinned) BEFORE entering the pipeline, and the pipeline rejects non-conforming input. That way implementations never normalize differently mid-stream.
   - Multi-set resolution rule: how does a meta-token resolve meaning across token sets? Define equivalence classes: within a frontier expansion, the scout produces K parallel tokenizations T1..K of the same logical span. Each Ti yields a sequence of (token_id, span_bytes) pairs. The meta-token groups by identical span_bytes coverage: a meta-token exists iff every token set covers exactly the same underlying byte range [start,end) in the source document, and the union of spans tiles the range without gaps/overlaps per set. Then the anchor is: AnchorID = H("MT1", doc_id, range, payload_hash, set_bindings...) — need care: bindings vary by set count; sort by TokenSetID.
   - Root accumulation: Merkle mountain range (MMR) or a simple append-only Merkle tree with leaves = sealed block records; each block = batch of meta-tokens from one scout burn. Root after N blocks is deterministic given the same sequence of blocks. Since scouts may run in nondeterministic wall-clock order across implementations, the ROOT can differ unless ordering is pinned. So the design must pin ordering: blocks ordered by (parent_root, first_meta_token_anchor_id)? Or better: make the root order-insensitive via a commutative accumulator? But Merkle roots depend on order. Options:
     a) Pin total order: sort all burns by a deterministic key derived from content, not arrival time (arrival time differs between implementations). E.g., each burn's BlockID = H(block content); order blocks by ascending BlockID bytes. Then root = Merkle over blocks sorted by BlockID. Two implementations processing the same frontier graph will emit the same SET of burns; sorting by BlockID gives identical sequences → identical roots. That's clean and fully content-addressed. Cost: can't stream incrementally in arrival order, but you can buffer per-frontier-batch and finalize at batch boundaries (deterministic batch boundaries: e.g., when frontier level L completes — BFS levels are content-determined).
     b) Use a commutative hash accumulator (multiset hash like XOR of leaf hashes — bad: malleable/collision-prone under adversarial dupes but fine here since leaves themselves are hashed and unique; still, XOR-based multiset hashing has known issues; better: sum in Z_p of H(leaf)^k? Overkill).
   - Option (a) with level-synchronous batches is concrete and defensible: frontier-scout pipelines naturally run level-by-level (frontier = current wave). Pin: process frontier waves in BFS order; within a wave, all burns collected; sort burns by BlockID ascending (32-byte lexicographic); build Merkle tree over sorted leaves; concatenate previous root; new root = H(prev_root || Merkle_root(wave)). Chain of roots per wave. Final root after all waves. Two independent implementations exploring the same start produce identical wave sets (if exploration itself is deterministic — need to pin expansion order and dedup rules too!).

Wait — deeper: "from the same start" — the two implementations run the whole pipeline from the same initial state. For roots to match, EVERYTHING must be deterministic: scout expansion order, tie-breaking on frontier selection, deduplication of visited states, tokenization (pinned tokenizer versions), and the meta-token construction. So my answer must cover the full determinism stack, then zoom into the meta-token as the keystone.

Also "burn": after sealing a scout's block into the wave tree, the scout's working memory is destroyed (burned); recovery is possible only via the anchored meta-tokens (content-addressed, so you can re-fetch/recompute). The anchor must therefore be self-sufficient: enough info to reconstruct meaning later without the burned context. That motivates carrying the canonical byte payload inside the meta-token (or its hash plus a locator). Byte-exactness demands we store the payload bytes or commit to them; storing full bytes makes the anchor verifiable standalone (H(payload) checkable).

Now let me nail down the exact spec. I'll write it like a mini-RFC. Concrete numbers, exact encodings. No fluff.

=== SPEC DRAFT ===

**Name:** MTX-1 (Meta-Token eXchange, v1). Or "ox-meta-token v1". Keep it tight.

**Primitives**
- Hash: BLAKE3, 32-byte output, keyed mode unused, extended mode unused. Domain separation via first-class prefix bytes in every preimage (not via BLAKE3 "context" string API? Actually BLAKE3's keyed_hash / derive_key contexts are fine and standard, but to keep both implementations trivially aligned, do manual prefixing with ASCII tags and plain BLAKE3 hash of the concatenated preimage. Manual prefixing is the least surprising cross-implementation choice.) All multi-part preimages: tag || len(field) || field with lengths as u64 big-endian? If every part is self-delimiting (tagged with explicit length), concatenation is injective → no ambiguity. Rule: every variable-length element is preceded by its u64-BE byte length. Fixed-size elements (u16/u32/u64, 32-byte hashes) written big-endian/fixed. This gives an injective canonical encoding with zero parser ambiguity.

**TokenSet descriptor (TSD)** — pins what a "token set" is:
```
tsd := {
  family_id:    ascii tag, ≤31 bytes, e.g. "bpe-v3"
  vocab_digest: 32B = H(vocab_file_canonical_bytes)
  merge_rules_digest: 32B (0^32 if none)
  special_tokens: sorted list of (ascii name, token_id u32)
  unicode_version: u32 major*1000+minor (e.g., 15*1000+0=15000) — actually simpler: u16 major, u16 minor
  flags: u8 bitfield
}
TokenSetID = H(T("TS1") || tsd)
```
Canonical tsd serialization: fixed field order, strings length-prefixed, lists length-prefixed with elements sorted by (name bytes) — names must be unique; reject duplicates.

**Logical span**: a byte range [off, off+len) in a canonical source artifact. Source artifact identified by ArtifactID = H(T("ART") || artifact_descriptor). Artifact descriptor includes content digest (so content-addressed), media type tag, and optional NFC-normalization proof flag. Rule: artifacts MUST be byte-stable (immutable); if text, MUST be NFC (Unicode version pinned by the TSD set used; if multiple sets with different Unicode versions touch one artifact — reject: artifact carries required_unicode_version and all sets must match).

Hmm wait — should the meta-token reference the artifact bytes or embed the payload? Embedding payload makes anchor self-contained; referencing makes it light. Do BOTH: embed `payload` (the exact bytes of the logical unit) AND ArtifactID + offsets. Verifier checks H(payload) against embedded digest and optionally against artifact slice. Self-contained wins for the burn scenario (artifact may be evicted too).

**Meta-token v1 wire format** — canonical TLV, top-level:

```
METATOKEN :=
  magic        "OMTX" (4 bytes ASCII)
  version      u16 = 1
  body_len     u64  (length of everything following, incl. trailing tag? decide: body_len covers fields through end of bindings; then trailer hash outside? Cleaner: whole record is self-hashing except the id field.)
```

Better construction to avoid self-reference: 
- Compute `body` = canonical encoding of all fields EXCEPT `id`.
- `id = MetaTokenID = H(T("MT1") || version_be16 || body)`
- Wire record = `magic || version || id || body`. Parsing recovers body, recomputes id, compares. Byte-identity of records ⟺ byte-identity of bodies ⟺ equal ids. 

Body fields, FIXED ORDER (order is normative; unknown trailing fields forbidden — forward compat via version bump only):

```
body :=
  u64  payload_len
  ...  payload bytes            (the canonical logical unit bytes)
  32B  payload_check            = H(T("PAY") || payload)   -- redundant but cheap verification
  32B  artifact_id              (may be 0^32 = "unbound")
  u64  span_off                 (byte offset in artifact; 0 if unbound)
  u64  span_len                 (== payload_len if bound; else arbitrary? NO — force equality or unbound-zero. Rule: if artifact_id == 0^32 then span_off==span_len==0 else span_len == payload_len. Enforce.)
  u32  kind                     (enum: 0=reserved,1=text-span,2=code-unit,3=structural,4=sentinel/end-of-stream,5=control/barrier,6=numeric-literal,7=opaque-bytes; others invalid in v1)
  u32  flags                    bitfield: bit0 = terminal-of-stream, bit1 = barrier (blocks merges across), bit2 = numeric-canonical-form present, bits3..31 reserved zero
  u64  seq                      — NO! seq would encode arrival order → nondeterminism across impls? Not necessarily: if seq is defined as position within the scout's canonical traversal order (content-determined), it's fine. But safer to exclude mutable/order-ish fields from identity and keep them in the BLOCK layer. Decision: NO seq in meta-token. Position within a stream is expressed by the parent STRUCTURE (a StreamBinding list), not by the token itself.
  bindings: u32 n_sets, then n_sets entries, EACH:
      32B  token_set_id
      u32  k_i = number of token ids realizing this unit in that set
      k_i × u32 token_ids   (MUST be sorted ascending, duplicates rejected — a set realizes a unit by a *set* of ids; ordering irrelevant to meaning so we canonicalize ascending)
      u64  tspan_off_i, u64 tspan_len_i : the sub-range of the artifact covered by those ids (must tile-check: for the binding to be valid, ∪ over consecutive units' tspans in that set partitions the artifact region claimed by the stream; checked at stream level, not token level)
```

Validity rules (all enforced; violations ⇒ reject record, do not silently fix):
1. n_sets ≥ 1.
2. token_set_ids strictly ascending (they're hashes; ascending byte order; uniqueness implied).
3. Within each binding, token_ids strictly ascending, k_i ≥ 1.
4. Bound case: payload_len == span_len ≥ 1.
5. kind ∈ {1..7}; reserved flag bits zero.
6. payload nonempty unless kind ∈ {4,5} (sentinels may be empty).
7. payload_check correct.
8. If kind == 6 (numeric), flags.bit2 == 1 and payload is the canonical decimal form defined below (see Numeric canon).

**Numeric canon (kind=6):** payload = ASCII decimal, integer form `-?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)`, no leading zeros, no plus sign; fractional form additionally `.d+` after integer part with no trailing zeros beyond necessity (strip trailing zeros in fraction; "1.5" ok, "1.50" rejected). Exponent form forbidden in v1 (forces writers to expand). This kills float formatting divergence (the classic 0.1+0.2 problem) by banning floats at the anchor boundary.

**Text canon:** payload is UTF-8 of NFC-normalized text; NFC Unicode version must equal the max unicode_version among bound sets (and artifact's declared version). Reject otherwise. (Enforce at ingest; implementations must NOT re-normalize — they validate.)

**Multi-set resolution semantics (the "anchor resolving meaning"):**
A meta-token asserts: "logical unit L (bytes = payload) is realized in token set S_i by exactly the id-multiset {t_{i,1..k}} covering artifact bytes [span_off, span_off+span_len)." Meaning-resolution rule for downstream consumers: given query token (S_q, t_q) appearing inside a bound region, resolve by looking up the stream index: find the meta-token whose S_q-binding contains t_q at the matching tspan position; the unit's meaning = payload (+ kind). Ambiguity guard: a given (S_q, t_q, absolute artifact offset) maps to AT MOST ONE meta-token — enforced at stream seal time by the tiling check. Cross-set alignment is then transitive through the shared payload/artifact coordinates: S_1's token ↔ offset range ↔ S_2's tokens. That's the anchor: artifact byte-coordinate space is the pivot; payload is the portable meaning; ids are per-set projections.

Edge cases to pin:
- A single token in S_a spanning bytes that S_b splits into three tokens: fine — k_b=3, tspan_b covers same range.
- Zero-width tokens (some tokenizers emit boundary markers): forbid in v1 — every id in a binding must cover ≥1 byte of the tspan. (Zero-width specials like chat-template markers belong to kind 5 control records OUTSIDE the anchored stream, carried in the block header, not as meta-tokens. Keeps the tiling invariant clean.)
- Same id appearing twice in a set's realization (repeated token): allowed ONLY if positions differ; but our binding is a set of ids + one tspan, losing positions! Problem: BPE ids repeat ("e" appears many times). Fix: binding entries are (token_id u32, rel_off u64, rel_len u64) triples relative to span_off — i.e., the exact tiling of the tspan by that set. Then repeats are fine, zero-width banned, and the tiling is explicit and checkable. YES — replace bare id lists with id+subrange triples. Sorted ascending by (rel_off, rel_len, token_id). Contiguity check: first triple rel_off=0; each next rel_off == prev rel_off+prev rel_len; last ends at span_len. Strict partition — gaps/overlaps rejected. This is the load-bearing invariant making cross-set resolution exact.

Revised binding entry:
```
binding :=
  32B  token_set_id
  u32  m_i            number of pieces
  m_i × piece:
     u32 token_id
     u64 rel_off
     u64 rel_len          (≥1)
pieces sorted by rel_off asc (then rel_len asc, then token_id asc — though contiguity makes ties impossible: consecutive rel_off differ, and equal rel_off impossible after first; so effectively sorted by rel_off alone; keep tiebreakers anyway as belt-and-braces, they're free)
```

**Streams & blocks (burn pipeline integration):**

A ScoutBurn produces one STREAM: the ordered sequence of meta-tokens emitted during one frontier-node processing, plus a header. Order within a stream is the scout's CANONICAL emission order — must be content-determined. Pin it: emission order = ascending artifact span order (by span_off, then span_len, then id bytes) for anchored units; control/sentinel records interleave per the canonical grammar of the node type (grammar pinned by node_type enum in header). Simplest universal rule: ALL meta-tokens in a stream sorted by (span_off, span_len, MetaTokenID). Control barriers (kind 5) get span_off of the barrier point. This makes stream order a pure function of content. 

Stream header:
```
hdr :=
  32B  prev_block_root       (chained; 0^32 for genesis wave)
  32B  node_state_in         (hash of frontier node's canonical state BEFORE processing)
  32B  node_state_out        (hash of successor frontier states' multiset commitment — see below)
  u32  node_type             (pinned enum)
  u32  n_tokens_total        (sum of m_i across all bindings — sanity bound)
  u32  n_records
```

Successor multiset commitment: scouts spawn successors; the SET of successor states matters, order doesn't (they'll be re-enqueued into the frontier which sorts them). Commit as: succ_root = H(T("SUCC") || Σ over successors of H(child_state) sorted ascending, length-prefixed list). Frontier itself is a priority queue keyed by (node_state_in hash asc) — pop order content-determined. 

Wave batching & THE ROOT:

Pipeline runs in waves. Wave w: drain frontier completely (pop in canonical priority order until empty), each pop → scout processes node → emits stream → enqueues successors (they form next wave's frontier; dedup: a node_state seen in ANY earlier wave at same-or-shallower depth is skipped — depth-keyed dedup, pin: skip if state hash seen at depth ≤ d). After wave drains: 
- Collect all streams of the wave. Sort streams by (first-record MetaTokenID asc, then whole-stream byte compare) — simplest: sort streams by their StreamID = H(T("STRM") || hdr || records) ascending; ties impossible (collision). 
- Wave leaf list = [StreamID_1..StreamID_n] sorted ascending. Merkleize: pairwise H(T("NODE")||L||R), odd leaf duplicated (Bitcoin-style, pinned), up to single root. Empty wave (n=0): root = 0^32 (and pipeline halts — frontier exhausted).
- Chained: wave_root_w = H(T("WAVE")||w_be_u64||prev_wave_root||merkle_root). Genesis prev = 0^32, w starts 0.
- FINAL ROOT = last wave_root. Also publish per-wave roots (audit chain).

Determinism argument, explicitly: two implementations from identical start (same artifact bytes, same TSD set, same node_type start state):
- Same artifact/TSD ⇒ same IDs.
- Frontier pops by hash order ⇒ same pop sequence.
- Scout processing is pure function of (node state, artifact, TSDs) ⇒ same emissions. (Pin: scout logic version-tagged in genesis params; any change bumps pipeline version.)
- Dedup by (state hash, depth) ⇒ same visited set.
- Streams sorted by content ⇒ same wave leaf order.
- Merkle + chaining fixed ⇒ identical wave roots ⇒ identical final root, byte-for-byte.

Non-determinism kill-list (state each explicitly — these are the classic byte-divergence sources):
- Floats: banned at anchor (numeric canon). No float anywhere in pipeline state; scores for frontier priority must derive from content (hash order), not learned scores — OR learned scores must be quantized to fixed-point u64 with pinned rounding. Default v1: hash-priority only.
- Map iteration: every collection either sorted canonically or a fixed-order list; no hash-map order leaks into any preimage.
- Time/randomness: no timestamps, no RNG in anything hashed. (Wall-clock may exist in logs; logs are not hashed.)
- Unicode: validated-NFC-at-ingest only; versions pinned per TSD; mismatch ⇒ reject.
- Locale/encoding: all lengths byte counts; all strings ASCII tags; no locale-dependent formatting anywhere.
- Parallelism: allowed freely — results are order-insensitive until wave-finalize, which is a deterministic sort. Burn (memory destruction) happens per-node right after its stream is sealed and locally verified (id recompute + tiling checks); nothing burned feeds a preimage later.
- Truncation/overflow: u64 offsets; reject artifact > 2^63 bytes; reject m_i > 2^24 per binding; reject n_sets > 4096; reject n_records > 2^20 per stream. Explicit limits prevent implementation-specific OOM behavior diverging.

Also define the "resolve" API concretely:
resolve(stream_index, S_q, token_id, abs_off) → MetaToken | NOT_FOUND:
  candidates = index[(S_q)] bucket by token_id; filter pieces where rel_off ≤ (abs_off − span_off) < rel_off+rel_len; assert exactly ≤1 candidate (seal-time invariant guarantees ≤1; runtime double-checks and fails loud on violation).

Exact, total (within sealed streams), no fuzzy matching anywhere. That's the "one anchor resolving meaning across multiple token sets."

Why content-addressing pays in burn: after burn, only IDs survive; any verifier holding artifact + TSDs can rebuild expected IDs and confirm the burned work happened (receipt property); any consumer can rehydrate meaning from ID→record stores without trusting scout memory. Re-derivation is the trust model.
